extracted.intended_audience: registered patent attorneys, respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings, disciplinary counsel, and USPTO OED staff
extracted.subtask_description: A Final Order under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 implementing reciprocal discipline where the USPTO imposes discipline identical to that imposed by a state disciplinary authority. Covers notice, opportunity to respond, standard if no response, and publication/notification requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predicate for reciprocal discipline (state discipline)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reciprocal discipline may be imposed when discipline by a State is the predicate (here, reproval by the State Bar Court of California).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This notice states the reprimand is "predicated upon being reproved by the State Bar Court of California, a duly constituted authority of a State." The USPTO may impose reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by the State Bar Court pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and opportunity to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must send a Notice and Order by certified mail informing the respondent that a Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline has been filed and providing an opportunity to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order here was sent by certified mail (receipt no. 70140510000082456102) and delivered to Respondent on February 12, 2018. The Notice provided the Respondent an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing the imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by the State Bar Court based on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible grounds to oppose reciprocal discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent may oppose imposition of identical reciprocal discipline based on the reasons enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order references that a response may oppose reciprocal discipline "based on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1)." (The Order does not restate the specific subsection text but preserves the respondent's right to raise those regulatory defenses.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of failure to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent fails to file a response to the Notice and Order, there is no genuine issue of material fact and reciprocal discipline may be imposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order states: "In light of Respondent's failure to file a response, it is hereby determined that there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and reprimanding Respondent is the appropriate discipline."

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate discipline: identical/reciprocal discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO will impose discipline identical to that imposed by the state authority (reciprocal discipline), here a public reprimand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order: "Respondent is hereby publicly reprimanded." The proceeding sought "reciprocal discipline upon Respondent identical to the discipline imposed by the State Bar Court of California."

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication in Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must publish a Notice in the Official Gazette describing the public discipline and the reasons for it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order directs: "The OED Director publish the following Notice in the Official Gazette" and provides the exact text of the Notice of Public Reprimand to be published, including facts about the State Bar reproval and the nature of the misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to disciplinary agencies, courts, and the public (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must give notice of the public discipline and reasons to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state(s) where the respondent is admitted, to courts where admitted, and to the public as required by regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order requires: "The OED Director give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state(s) where Respondent is admitted to practice, to courts ... and to the public."

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of misconduct warranting reproval (commingling client funds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific misconduct cited as the basis for the State Bar reproval: depositing and commingling personal funds in client trust account and issuing checks from trust account for non-client related purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice text describes: "Mr. Jew was publicly reproved by the State Bar Court of California for depositing and commingling his personal funds in his client trust account, and issuing fourteen checks from his trust account for non-client related purposes." This illustrates the kind of trust-account mismanagement that can lead to reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedial conditions imposed by the State (examples of corrective requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: The State Bar Court's reproval included additional remedial requirements the respondent was ordered to comply with within one year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order lists the State Bar's additional requirements as examples of remediation: "submitting quarterly reports to the Office of Probation of the State Bar of California affirming his compliance with the State Bar Act, the Rules of Professional Conduct, and reproval; attending Ethics School; passing the Multistate Professional Responsibility Examination; filing a certificate from a financial professional that he has maintained a trust account; and taking the course, Ethics School Client Trust Accounting School."

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and regulatory authority for discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary action is taken pursuant to statutory and regulatory provisions empowering the USPTO to discipline practitioners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites authority: "This action is taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24." It also references availability of disciplinary decisions via OED FOIA Reading Room: http://e-foia.uspto.gov/Foia/OEDReadingRoom.jsp.
